one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent chose to hardcode FEN-to-legal-moves mappings for individual positions in re.json rather than synthesizing a general regex-based chess move generator, then fell into a position-by-position debugging loop (including a regressive removal of the starting-position mapping at step 38) that never converged on a broadly correct solution.
t_err_evidence: At step 20 the agent creates re.json with a single hardcoded regex entry that exactly matches one specific FEN string and maps it to three precomputed result positions — acting on the false premise that enumerating individual positions could satisfy the task's requirement for a general move generator across arbitrary chess positions.
t_commit_evidence: At step 45 the agent creates 'analyze_position2.py' targeted at position-by-position extraction and explicitly decides to continue the overfitted pattern of analyzing one failing FEN at a time, rather than pivoting to a general solution. By this point three positions are still failing and the agent's own step-42 think block acknowledges the approach 'won't scale' but proceeds with it anyway, locking in the losing trajectory.
t_surface_evidence: Step 23 runs check.py and shows 'Our moves: 1, Python-chess moves: 20' for the starting position — a clear observable signal that the current re.json produces no valid output for any unseen position.
trigger_explanation: The agent assumed without verification that a feasible path to passing the tests was to enumerate individual FEN→output mappings. It never considered that the task required a general regex pipeline capable of handling arbitrary positions, despite the check.py harness testing a whole game (17+ positions) and the task description implying generality. The hardcoding approach was structurally incapable of passing the benchmark.
forewarning_evidence: Step 23 shows 'Our moves: 1, Python-chess moves: 20' — the agent's solution returns only one 'move' (the unchanged FEN string) for the starting position. Steps 32 and 41 show repeated check.py failures on subsequent positions ('Our moves: 1, Python-chess moves: 29/27'), reinforcing that the approach cannot generalize. These signals all precede t_commit at step 45.
